pr_title: [e2e] Fix node port service reachability test for nodes running on localhost
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind failing-test

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

If a node's internal address points to 127.0.0.1, then we skip the node
port reachability test.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #80760

**Release note**:
```release-note
NONE
```

<!-- Please only use this template for submitting reports about failing tests in Kubernetes CI jobs -->

**Which jobs are failing**:

**Which test(s) are failing**:

/milestone v1.16
/assign @mgdevstack 
FYI

Looks like two other release-blocking tests too: https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-release-master-blocking#gce-cos-master-slow&width=20
- `[sig-network] ESIPP [Slow] [DisabledForLargeClusters] should work from pods`
- `[sig-network] Services should only allow access from service loadbalancer source ranges [Slow]`

The changes link testgrid gives (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/compare/acd597dba...9aefaa163) suggests two other PR's, but I agree that https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/79667 seems the likely culprit

>1. [sig-network] ESIPP [Slow] [DisabledForLargeClusters] should work from pods
>2. [sig-network] Services should only allow access from service loadbalancer source ranges [Slow]

`execPod := e2epod.CreateExecPodOrFail()` seems flaky to me. Most of time execPod starts running and might be terminating immediately after some time which causes this issue. 

[1.] e2e is failing as `acceptPod := e2epod.CreateExecPodOrFail(cs, namespace, "execpod-accept", nil)` might have terminated and so no PodIP leading to invalid `svc.Spec.LoadBalancerSourceRanges`.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9aefaa163f9a8a397de20f4acd41aa25658e9133/test/e2e/network/service.go#L1480
[2.] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9aefaa163f9a8a397de20f4acd41aa25658e9133/test/e2e/network/service.go#L2203
empty `execPod.Status.PodIP`.

The same issue had been observed in #79667 for `[sig-network] Services [It] should preserve source pod IP for traffic thru service cluster IP` E2E and to fix the issue, we introduced execPod deployment to make sure execPod would remain in desired running state.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9aefaa163f9a8a397de20f4acd41aa25658e9133/test/e2e/framework/service/jig.go#L1146

It's better to address this change in another PR and emphasize using pausePod deployment.

Thanks, @saschagrunert for helping me setting up CRI-O based cluster.

>1. Kubernetes e2e suite [sig-network] Services should be able to change the type from ExternalName to NodePort
2. Kubernetes e2e suite [sig-network] Services should be able to create a functioning NodePort service 19s

From log, it is clear that, these services are failing to reach over allocated nodePort. But on my CRIO based testing cluster, they are reachable. 
@saschagrunert or @mrunalp, Could you please check if they failing at your end too or it's testgrid Job-specific issue?

@saschagrunert Thanks for reproducing this. FYI we've seem similar failure on https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/81000, but I haven't reproduced the problem locally yet.

We are looking to at least turn on verbose on the test command for debugging: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/81049.

The issue is that we try to automatically discover the node IP by obtaining its status here:

https://github.com/mgdevstack/kubernetes/blob/1438a3c8fc88d6422b716326dc8f9b19921743f5/test/e2e/framework/service/jig.go#L772-L781

In our setup the node has IP `127.0.0.1` which for sure does not work if we try to access it within the pod. I'm thinking about a proper solution and will propose it as a PR.
